(a) Joint Process for Technical Compliance and Quality Control.—If the Secretary of a military department transfers any maintenance action on a platform to a depot under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of another military department, the two Secretaries shall develop and implement a process to ensure the technical compliance and quality control for the work performed. 
    (b) Requirements.—A process developed under subsection (a) shall include the following requirements—
        (1) The Secretary of the military department with jurisdiction over the depot to which the maintenance action is transferred shall—
            (A) ensure that the technical specifications, requirements, and standards for work to be performed are provided to such action or depot; and 
            (B) implement procedures to ensure that completed work complies with such specifications, requirements and standards.  
        (2) The Secretary who transfers the maintenance activity or depot shall ensure that—
            (A) the technical specifications and requirements are clearly understood; and 
            (B) the work performed is completed to the technical specifications, requirements, and standards prescribed under paragraph (1), and that the Secretary of the military department with jurisdiction over the depot is informed of any shortcoming or discrepancy.   
    (c) Reports.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report containing a certification that sufficient policy and procedures are in place to ensure quality control when the depot or maintenance activities of one military department support another. The report shall include a description of known shortfalls in existing policies and procedures and actions the Department of Defense is taking to address such shortfalls.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a jointly developed process and a required report amount to consultation or coordination. Both stay inside the federal government: the joint process is between the Secretaries of two military departments, and the report goes to the congressional defense committees. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is brought into any federal decision, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: the two Secretaries shall develop and implement a process to ensure the technical compliance and quality control for the work performed.

qwen_block.w: The section requires coordination and process development between two Secretaries of military departments. Both the Secretary of one military department and the Secretary of another are federal officials inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities. The report mentioned in subsection (c) is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: If the Secretary of a military department transfers any maintenance action on a platform to a depot under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of another military department, the two Secretaries shall develop and implement a process to ensure the technical compliance and quality control for the work performed.

opus.w: Everyone involved here is inside the federal government. The Secretaries of two military departments work out a joint quality-control process, and the Under Secretary of Defense reports to the congressional defense committees. The words "joint process" and "reports" sound procedural, but working together within the Department of Defense and reporting to Congress are both listed traps, so they don't count. No state, company, expert, or member of the public takes part in any decision.
opus.s: the two Secretaries shall develop and implement a process to ensure the technical compliance and quality control for the work performed.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires coordination between two federal officials (Secretaries of military departments) to develop a process for maintenance actions. Since both actors are inside the federal government, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties. The report to Congress is also an internal government action.
qwen_chat.s: If the Secretary of a military department transfers any maintenance action on a platform to a depot under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of another military department, the two Secretaries shall develop and implement a process to ensure the technical compliance and quality control for the work performed.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for two Secretaries to "develop and implement a process" constitutes coordination or consultation. However, both the Secretary of one military department and the Secretary of another military department are federal officials inside the executive branch. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is not participation. Furthermore, the report mentioned in subsection (c) is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no involvement of states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities in the decision-making process described.
